intro.welcome: Welcome to the Countries Geo documentation, your one-stop solution for accessing continents, countries, states and cities information.
intro.availableInfoDesc: Explore the different areas you can access with enhanced data including ISO2/ISO3 codes, telephone codes, coordinates, and multi-language support:
intro.continentDesc: Continents are the largest landmasses on Earth, typically divided into seven regions: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and Australia. These vast areas are distinguished by geographical boundaries, cultural differences, and unique ecosystems.
intro.continentNew: Now includes ISO2/ISO3 codes, coordinates, and multi-language names.
intro.countriesDesc: Countries are sovereign political entities with defined borders, governments, and populations. Each country has its own laws, currency, and identity, such as the United States, Brazil, or Japan.
intro.countriesNew: Now includes ISO2/ISO3 codes, telephone codes, coordinates, and multi-language names.
intro.statesDesc: States/Regions are subdivisions within a country that help with administrative and political organization. For example, the U.S. has 50 states, India has 28 states, and Germany has 16 federal states.
intro.statesNew: Now includes coordinates and multi-language names.
intro.citiesDesc: Cities/Towns are populated urban or semi-urban areas within a country, serving as centers for commerce, culture, and governance.
intro.citiesNew: Now includes coordinates and multi-language names.

why.dataText: ISO2/ISO3 codes, telephone codes, coordinates, and multi-language names for comprehensive geographic data
why.docsText: Detailed guides and reference material to help you integrate with our services effortlessly.
why.scaleText: Build applications that scale with your business, from small projects to large enterprise solutions.
why.securityText: Rest assured with our robust security protocols, ensuring your integrations and data are always protected.

include.isoText: Standard international codes for better compatibility
include.coorText: Latitude and longitude for precise geographic location
include.namesText: Support for names in multiple languages

intro.backwardCompatDesc: The library maintains full backward compatibility while providing access to enhanced features:
intro.closing: Whether you're a seasoned developer or just starting out, this is designed to provide a clear understanding of how to use this utility tool.
intro.faqIntro: The Countries Geo FAQ is a collection of useful questions and answers about the project. If you have a question that isn't answered here, please <discussions>open a discussion</discussions>.
intro.q1: Can I use Countries Geo with my Javascript Project?
intro.a1: Countries Geo would work on any javascript project so far as its node based.
intro.q2: Do I have to pay for this service?
intro.a2: Countries Geo is open-source and free to use for any kind of project:
intro.a2Point1: There is currently no plan now or in the future to charge for this service.
intro.a2Point2: Though a channel could be provided in the future for individuals or companies that would want to support with a donation
intro.q3: How do I suggest the addition of missing data?
intro.a3: Use the <report>missing or wrong place form</report> on GitHub. A GeoNames or Wikidata link helps us verify and add the place quickly.

roadmap.title: Our Roadmap
roadmap.searchDesc: Find continents, countries, states and cities by name, ignoring accents and case, in any loaded language.
roadmap.currenciesDesc: Add each country's ISO 4217 currencies and ISO 639 official languages.
roadmap.flagsDesc: Ship a flag emoji for every country, with SVG flags as an optional separate import.
roadmap.bordersDesc: List the countries that share a land border with a given country.
roadmap.nearestCityDesc: Find the closest city to a latitude and longitude, using the coordinates already in the dataset.
roadmap.populationDesc: Add population figures for countries and cities, and land area for countries.
roadmap.cityNamesDesc: Translate more city names, since coverage currently varies by language and country.
